anatomy.title: Anatomia
anatomy.item1: Raiz — agrupa as partes e guarda os valores, a faixa e a orientação.
anatomy.item2: Área de interação — captura arrasto e teclado sobre toda a extensão do trilho, e não só sobre a alça.
anatomy.item3: Trilho — a barra de fundo sobre a qual o preenchimento corre.
anatomy.item4: Preenchimento — o segmento cheio: do início da faixa até a alça, ou entre as duas alças num intervalo.
anatomy.item5: Alça — o pegador, com role="slider" e aria-valuenow. Uma por valor.

structureCode.react:

/>

{/* Range (dois thumbs) */}

  value={[20, 80]}

guidelines.title: Guidelines Obrigatórias
guidelines.item1: Use para valores numéricos contínuos onde a granularidade exata não importa.
guidelines.item2: Forneça aria-label ou aria-labelledby descrevendo o valor controlado.
guidelines.item3: Mostre o valor atual textualmente próximo ao slider — usuários precisam confirmar.
guidelines.item4: Para input exato de número, use Input type="number" em vez de Slider.

notes.title: Notas de Implementação
notes.item1: Duas anatomias para a alça — ora ela envolve um <input type="range">, que já traz papel e limites do navegador, ora ela mesma é o elemento focável, com os limites escritos em ARIA. As duas anunciam a mesma coisa ao leitor de tela; asserção que exige uma delas reprova a outra sem que nada esteja quebrado.
notes.item2: Array de valores — value e defaultValue são sempre arrays, mesmo para um valor só ([50]).
notes.item3: Mudança contínua vs valor confirmado — o callback de mudança dispara durante arrasto; use o callback de commit (ao soltar) para analytics e submit, evitando spam.
notes.item4: Vertical — o componente já tem altura mínima própria em pé; defina a altura no container quando quiser um trilho mais longo.

anatomy.title: Anatomy
anatomy.item1: Root — groups the parts and holds the values, the range and the orientation.
anatomy.item2: Interaction area — captures drag and keyboard along the whole track, not only over the thumb.
anatomy.item3: Track — the background bar over which the fill runs.
anatomy.item4: Fill — the filled segment: from the start of the range to the thumb, or between the two thumbs in a range.
anatomy.item5: Thumb — the grabber, with role="slider" and aria-valuenow. One per value.

guidelines.title: Required Guidelines
guidelines.item1: Use for continuous numeric values where exact granularity doesn't matter.
guidelines.item2: Provide aria-label or aria-labelledby describing the controlled value.
guidelines.item3: Display the current value textually near the slider — users need to confirm.
guidelines.item4: For exact number input, use Input type="number" instead of Slider.

ariaLabel.name: aria-label

range.name: Range (two thumbs)
range.format: Min and Max separated by em-dash

do.title: Use when
do.item1: The value is continuous and exact granularity is secondary
do.item2: Visualizing position on the range matters to the user
do.item3: The user needs to select a range (min/max)
do.item4: Tactile/visual interaction is more intuitive than typing

dont.title: Do not use when
dont.item1: User needs to input an exact value — use Input type="number"
dont.item2: There are 2-3 discrete options — use RadioGroup or ToggleGroup
dont.item4: Range is very wide (1-10000) and requires precision — combine Input + Slider

hover.label: Hover

focus.label: Focus
focus.behavior: Keyboard focused — the thumb border switches to ring and gains an outer ring in the same colour; arrows, Home and End change the value.

active.label: Active
active.behavior: While dragging — the thumb follows the pointer and the fill grows with it, the value changing on every move.

notes.title: Implementation Notes
notes.item1: Two anatomies for the thumb — sometimes it wraps an <input type="range">, which already brings role and bounds from the browser; sometimes the thumb itself is the focusable element, with the bounds written in ARIA. Both announce the same thing to a screen reader; an assertion that demands one of them fails the other with nothing broken.
notes.item2: Value array — value and defaultValue are always arrays, even for a single value ([50]).
notes.item3: Continuous change vs committed value — the change callback fires during drag; use the commit callback (on release) for analytics and submit to avoid spam.
notes.item4: Vertical — the component already has its own minimum height when upright; set the height on the container when you want a longer track.

slider_change.trigger: Value committed (drag end or keyup) — use the commit callback, not the continuous one
slider_change.payload: { component: "slider", field_name, value, min, max, location }

item2.result: Fires the commit callback with the final value

accessibility.item2: Minimum 3:1 contrast between the thumb border and the track
